description: When a team or system issue prevents me from practicing according to our standards of care, I promptly loop in my office manager, regional manager, or Clinical Director so the issue can be addressed appropriately.

action_statement: I always ask parents "what matters most to you about your child's dental care and the experience they have with us"- Before Discussing Treatment Options
description:
When discussing treatment recommendations—especially when there are areas of concern—I ask parents what matters most to them about their child’s dental care and experience before presenting options.

This helps ensure the conversation is aligned with the family’s priorities and allows recommendations to be framed in a way that feels collaborative and thoughtful.

action_statement: I always align treatment recommendations with what the family identifies as most important.
description: When families hear their priorities reflected back, trust increases and resistance decreases.

action_statement: I always recommend sedation options based on what is safest and most likely to succeed for the child, while also considering what matters most to the family.
description:
I recommend sedation options based on what is safest and most likely to succeed for the child, while also considering what matters most to the family.

I begin with a clear professional recommendation and explanation, and then discuss other clinically appropriate options if families would like to explore them.

action_statement: I always perform a brief pre-treatment check-in with the parent to confirm the plan, set expectations, and reinforce our commitment to the child’s comfort before beginning care.
description:
At the beginning of treatment appointments, I perform a brief check-in with the parent to confirm the plan, set expectations, and reinforce our commitment to the child’s comfort before beginning care.

This conversation is concise—typically 1–2 minutes—and ensures families understand the plan for the visit and any reasonable variations that could occur during treatment.

action_statement: I always ensure a clear (mutually agreed upon) treatment plan is in place before leaving the room/conversation with parent and RDA.
description: While options may be discussed verbally, I direct the RDA to chart one clear treatment plan so the team and family leave with a shared understanding of what will happen next.

action_statement: I always briefly introduce our AI technology and explain our proactive philosophy of care during exam appointments.
description: When families understand how diagnoses are formed, they are more confident in recommendations.

action_statement: I always ensure the parent and RDA clearly understand the next appointment before leaving the room.
description: Unclear next steps commonly cause missed appointments, delayed treatment, and parent frustration.

action_statement: I always honor the existing treatment and sedation plan whenever possible
description:
When a patient is seen by a different provider, I carefully review the existing treatment and sedation plan and work to honor that plan whenever it remains clinically appropriate.

Before modifying a previously discussed or agreed-upon plan, I pause to consider the trust impact on the family and the alignment between providers, and ensure that any change is truly clinically necessary.

action_statement: I always introduce age-appropriate future recommendations early so families understand what to expect as their child grows.
description:
I introduce age-appropriate future recommendations early so families understand what to expect as their child grows.

This helps normalize future care milestones and ensures recommendations feel planned and intentional, rather than sudden or reactive.

action_statement: When a child is tolerating treatment well and time permits, I always ask the parent's permission mid-appointment to complete additional planned treatment the same day.
description: A good visit is a scarce resource; asking permission honors the parent's role while saving the family a trip and a sedation event.

action_statement: I always keep routine exams to about five minutes of doctor time.
description: Exam time is the doctor's scarcest resource and the schedule is built on it. Focus, not speed, is what families experience.

action_statement: I always keep nitrous appointments to no more than 20 minutes of treatment time.
description: Nitrous gives a limited cooperation window; procedures are scoped to fit it rather than the window stretched to fit the plan.

action_statement: I always keep oral sedation appointments to no more than 40 minutes of treatment time.
description: Oral sedation has a depth and duration window; working past it trades safety margin and the child's experience for production.

action_statement: I always keep parent conversations purposeful, warmly redirecting when they drift.
description: Parent conversation is the highest-value time in the visit, which is exactly why it deserves protection.

action_statement: Before stepping away from the clinical floor, I always make sure current patients have been attended to, the team has what they need, and no exams, checks, or clinical needs are waiting on me.
description: The clinical floor runs on the doctor's availability. Stepping away is fine; stepping away clean is the discipline.

action_statement: After presenting a treatment plan, I always ask the parent to share their understanding of the plan back to me, so I can fill any gaps before they leave.
description: Parents routinely leave with a different understanding than the doctor believes was communicated; the gap is cheap to fix only while everyone is still in the room.

action_statement: When presenting a treatment plan, I always give parents explicit permission to push back and invite them to explore alternatives with me.
description: Parents who will not voice doubts in the room vote with the schedule instead. Explicit permission moves the objection somewhere it can be addressed.

action_statement: When a parent declines recommended treatment, I always repeat their decision back out loud and ask a curious, open-ended question to better understand their rationale.
description: A decline met with pressure ends the conversation; a decline met with curiosity keeps the relationship and usually surfaces an addressable concern.

action_statement: When a parent communicates that cost is a barrier to care, I always ask whether there is a budget we should be mindful of, and whether they want to see every option we would recommend, including those insurance may not cover.
description: Cost is the most common unspoken driver of declined care, and families rarely raise it twice. Asking respects both their reality and their autonomy.

action_statement: When a parent communicates that cost is a barrier to care, I always acknowledge the concern without judgment, name the clinically sound alternatives that could change the cost, and personally connect the family with our treatment coordinator.
description: How the doctor handles the cost moment decides whether the family leaves with a path or a dead end.

action_statement: When a parent seems overwhelmed by findings or a plan, I always name what I am noticing out loud, normalize it, and ask an open question about what is going through their mind.
description: An overwhelmed parent has stopped absorbing information, and decisions made in that state do not hold. Naming stays vague on the emotion deliberately.
